3. What a scheduler may do — the policy space is three choices
Because no op splits a transition, the whole policy space is:
— among the ready Loci, which gets its next transition,
and in what order within a round.
— when a ready Locus is parked and no slot is free, which
resident Locus is evicted (parked) to make room; and whether a Locus that becomes ready while parked is installed at all.
— with several floors, on which floor a Locus is resident
(R6's movement, used as a policy lever).
Given a fixed atomic-transition and ready/admissible interface, ComputeDriven Locus Multiplexing exposes three scheduling control dimensions: selection, residency, and placement

(the wording frozen by the R7 adjudication, §12). Around the scheduler there is more — event production and readiness admission, deadlines, backpressure, priority, durability policy — but those feed the ready set or price the transition; they are not further multiplexing dimensions:
